sequences.title: From diploid germ cells to released sperm
sequences.mechanism: Somatic support permits germ-cell proliferation, meiotic reduction and differentiation; spermiation releases sperm into the tubule lumen.

steps.caption: Sertoli support and local testosterone sustain spermatogenesis.
steps.mechanism: Leydig cells supply testosterone; Sertoli cells support developing germ cells.

steps.caption: Spermatogonia divide in the basal compartment.
steps.mechanism: Mitotic progeny maintain the pool and enter differentiation.

steps.caption: After DNA replication, primary spermatocytes enter meiosis.
steps.mechanism: Replicated homologous chromosomes prepare for the first meiotic division.

steps.caption: Meiosis I separates homologous chromosomes.
steps.mechanism: Secondary spermatocytes are haploid, with replicated chromosomes.

steps.caption: Meiosis II separates sister chromatids.
steps.mechanism: Haploid spermatids result from the second division.

steps.caption: Spermiogenesis remodels spermatids without another division.
steps.mechanism: Nuclear condensation, acrosome and flagellum formation specialize the cell.

steps.caption: Spermiation releases sperm into the lumen.
steps.mechanism: Newly released sperm are carried onward in fluid; release differs from epididymal maturation.

schematic_limitations: Stages are illustrative snapshots, not animated division or transformation of mesh objects.
n denotes chromosome sets; c denotes relative DNA content. Existing cell counts are not yield measurements.
The single Germ cell nuclei part spans multiple stages; it is never assigned exclusively to one germ-cell stage.
Inset ~x200; sequence order is compressed and has no real-time duration, synchronization, age or hormone prediction.

sequences.title: Sertoli barrier and protected germ-cell transit
sequences.mechanism: Junctions between adjacent Sertoli cells establish distinct epithelial compartments; germ-cell progression is shown without junction motion.

steps.caption: The blood-testis barrier is a Sertoli-to-Sertoli junctional barrier.
steps.mechanism: The basement membrane and capillary wall are different structures.

steps.caption: Basal spermatogonia and later adluminal stages occupy different microenvironments.
steps.mechanism: Early primary spermatocytes transit toward the protected compartment.

schematic_limitations: No junction, basal space or adluminal-space mesh exists; selected Sertoli cells provide context for the caption only.
Do not imply all Primary spermatocytes are already adluminal or that the barrier globally opens.
Detailed junction remodeling is deferred because the primary full paper could not be opened.
No barrier opening, junction deformation or transiting-cell cyst is animated.

sequences.title: Testis to epididymal maturation and storage
sequences.mechanism: Fluid and duct-wall activity transport sperm; regional epididymal changes permit maturation before caudal storage.

steps.caption: Seminiferous outflow enters the straight tubules and rete.
steps.mechanism: The source combines tubuli recti and rete testis into one catalog part.

steps.caption: Efferent ductules connect the rete to the epididymal head.
steps.mechanism: This is a duct-continuity lesson; moving markers are not required.

steps.caption: Sperm mature while passing through the epididymis.
steps.mechanism: Smooth-muscle activity transports cells through the coiled duct.

steps.caption: Mature sperm are stored mainly in the epididymal tail.
steps.mechanism: Caudal storage precedes release into the ductus deferens.

steps.caption: During emission, contraction releases sperm into the ductus deferens.
steps.mechanism: Neural activation of the caudal muscular coat drives outflow.

schematic_limitations: Highlight order represents topology, not transit speed or autonomous sperm swimming within the male ducts.
Acquiring motility capacity differs from capacitation; fertilization and female tract events are outside this model.
~x200 and ~x1300 insets are not continuous-scale extensions of this tract.
No numerical transit time is encoded; example histology source is rat.

sequences.title: Emission: delivery and mixing in the posterior urethra
sequences.mechanism: Predominantly sympathetic activity recruits smooth muscle, delivers duct/gland contents and closes the bladder neck.

steps.caption: The bladder neck closes during emission.
steps.mechanism: Closure directs ejaculatory outflow away from the bladder.

steps.caption: Duct contraction delivers sperm toward the ampulla.
steps.mechanism: The epididymal tail and ductus deferens provide the sperm-bearing stream.

steps.caption: Seminal gland fluid joins the sperm-bearing stream.
steps.mechanism: The seminal-gland duct joins the ampulla to form the ejaculatory duct.

steps.caption: Ejaculatory ducts discharge into the prostatic urethra.
steps.mechanism: The colliculus is a local opening landmark, not a downstream duct segment.

steps.caption: Prostatic secretions enter the prostatic urethra.
steps.mechanism: Prostatic ducts add gland fluid to semen; they do not join the ejaculatory duct upstream.

schematic_limitations: Gland and duct secretion overlap physiologically; highlight order is a teaching decomposition, not exact fraction timing.
Prostatic and seminal gland ducts are not individually selectable; captions identify the missing connection.
The prostate zones are context for one gland; equal highlighting does not assert equal secretion.
Autonomic pathways and semen pressure/volume are not modeled.

sequences.title: Expulsion: rhythmic propulsion through the urethra
sequences.mechanism: Somatic activation produces rhythmic perineal contraction after emission, propelling semen through a coordinated urethral outlet.

steps.caption: Rhythmic bulbospongiosus activity supplies the expulsive drive.
steps.mechanism: The bladder neck remains closed; muscle highlighting stands for contraction.

steps.caption: The outlet coordinates passage into the intermediate urethra.
steps.mechanism: Urethral sphincter activity is coordinated with propulsion.

steps.caption: Semen passes through the spongy urethra.
steps.mechanism: The lumen within the corpus spongiosum is the outflow route.

steps.caption: The ejaculate leaves through the external urethral orifice.
steps.mechanism: This completes the antegrade tract pathway.

schematic_limitations: No imposed contraction frequency, fixed pulse count, pressure, deformation or sphincter waveform.
External sphincter is shown as coordinated, not arbitrarily held shut or assigned a universal continuous relaxation waveform.
Ejaculation and orgasm are distinct; no cerebral experience is animated.
Bulbourethral mucus on arousal is not an obligatory final semen-mixing step during expulsion.

sequences.title: Erection: increased inflow and reduced venous outflow
sequences.mechanism: Local NO signaling relaxes erectile smooth muscle, permits increased arterial inflow and promotes veno-occlusion.

steps.caption: NO-mediated smooth-muscle relaxation enables erection.
steps.mechanism: NO-dependent relaxation is supported by primary experimental work.

steps.caption: Increased arterial inflow fills the cavernous spaces.
steps.mechanism: The deep artery feeds the erectile tissue.

steps.caption: Expansion reduces venous outflow through subtunical venules.
steps.mechanism: The tunica constrains expansion; the named dorsal vein is drainage context.

steps.caption: The spongy urethra remains a distinct conduit.
steps.mechanism: Erectile tissue surrounds the duct; blood filling and urethral flow are different pathways.

schematic_limitations: Static selection only: no penile enlargement, compliance, pressure, deforming tunica or blood solver.
Cavernous nerves are absent. Do not use the Dorsal nerve of penis as a replacement parasympathetic motor pathway.
Veno-occlusion acts through distributed venular drainage; the Deep dorsal vein of penis is not depicted as a closable valve.
Erection and voiding are separate teaching modes, not a claim that erection alone absolutely prevents urination.

sequences.title: Voiding: coordinated bladder contraction and outlet relaxation
sequences.mechanism: Storage keeps the detrusor relaxed and outlet closed; voiding coordinates bladder contraction with sphincter relaxation.

steps.caption: Storage: relaxed bladder wall and closed outlet.
steps.mechanism: Sphincter activity prevents leakage during filling.

steps.caption: Voiding requires coordinated outlet relaxation.
steps.mechanism: Reduced sphincter resistance permits bladder outflow.

steps.caption: The detrusor contracts to drive urine into the urethra.
steps.mechanism: Bladder-wall contraction produces the driving force.

steps.caption: Urine uses the same urethral segments.
steps.mechanism: Urinary outflow uses the prostatic, intermediate and spongy urethra.

steps.caption: Urine exits at the external urethral orifice.
steps.mechanism: No reproductive gland route is activated by this lesson.

schematic_limitations: No urinary pressure, bladder volume, flow rate, neural feedback or emptying solver.
The urethral objects are wall/conduit selectors, not verified fluid volumes.
Outlet relaxation and detrusor contraction are coordinated physiology; separate highlights do not encode an obligatory measurable delay.
Switching mode must clear all previous selections and teaching state.

description_overrides.Acrosome: Acrosome: a Golgi-derived secretory cap over the anterior sperm nucleus. Acrosomal exocytosis releases contents and remodels the sperm head during fertilization. Capacitation, interaction with the cumulus and zona pellucida, and membrane fusion are distinct steps. Human zona recognition involves several molecular interactions; this inset does not depict a single universal ZP3 trigger or establish reaction timing.
description_overrides.Neck (centrioles) & post-acrosomal regio: Neck (connecting piece) and post-acrosomal region: the neck joins the head and flagellum. Human sperm retain a typical proximal centriole and a structurally remodeled atypical distal centriole near the axoneme base. Research supports functions for both in paternal centrosome contribution, with some functional evidence obtained from extract assays and bovine zygotes. The centrioles are not separately resolved by this teaching mesh. The post-acrosomal head region participates in the sperm-oocyte interaction.

head_provenance: Sperm head: representative flattened ellipsoid using reported mean length 5.18 um, width 3.53 um and volume 8.03 um^3. Thickness is calculated from an ellipsoid-volume assumption, not independently measured. Tail calibre and organelle visibility are exaggerated for teaching.

nuclear_ownership.mechanism: Same kind/c/rad/a/squash records generate each germ-cell body and its smaller nucleus after _space_cells. sg/sc1/sc2/sd/esd kinds map to Spermatogonia/Primary spermatocytes/Secondary spermatocytes/Spermatids/Spermatids.
nuclear_ownership.warning: Count inferred from put calls, not saved-mesh component count or histologic population. Existing merged nuclear mesh loses per-parent identity; emit deterministic parent record sidecar during construction if stage-specific nuclear isolation is required.

nuclear_ownership.mechanism: One basal oval nucleus per Sertoli sector; preserve same sector index in any future transform.
Use paired per-cell generation record, not nearest global mesh label. Exact count not asserted here.

anatomical_domains.required_rule: Do not reinterpret any whole solid label as fluid; retain authored inner/outer wall radii. Flow uses source-derived centerlines and explicit lumen sampling in deferred build.

anatomical_domains.semantic: neighboring material territories with legitimate fitted contacts
anatomical_domains.required_rule: No global pairwise collision elimination. Preserve zones, gland/duct contacts, capsule and posterior colliculus relationship. Existing approximate 70/25/5 glandular-zone labels are teaching proportions, not mesh-volume guarantees.

anatomical_domains.semantic: nested parent cell and nuclear material
anatomical_domains.required_rule: Cells and nuclei must co-transform, but displayed parent cytoplasm should not render through nuclei on the section plane. Semantic containment differs from material-domain exclusivity. Do not subtract nuclei from the whole tubule or force every nucleus into Sertoli.

anatomical_domains.semantic: whole luminal sperm representatives, despite category nucleus
anatomical_domains.required_rule: Preserve exact name/color and assign teaching sidecar semantic whole_sperm; do not treat this label as only nuclear material in automated ownership rules.
Do not use Inguinal canal translucent marker as bodily fluid or tissue and do not globally boolean it from neighboring layers.

anatomical_domains.semantic: composite basement membrane plus peritubular myoid shell
anatomical_domains.required_rule: Keep composite identity explicit; label does not prove separately resolved basal lamina and myoid cells.

anatomical_domains.semantic: organelles and sheaths in independently enlarged sperm inset
anatomical_domains.required_rule: Keep all independent domains and head-tail attachment; avoid tissue texture creating additional nuclei. 9+2 motif is educational ultrastructure, not native nanometre geometry.
